title: I Love the Windows of Thy Grace
description: I Love the Windows of Thy Grace in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 145, headed “Sight through a glass, and face to face”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I love the win-dows of thy grace Thro' which my Lord is seen, And long to meet my Sav-iour's face With-out a glass be-tween.

lines: I love the windows of thy grace
Thro' which my Lord is seen,
And long to meet my Saviour's face
O, that the happy hour were come
To change my faith to sight!
I shall behold my Lord at home
Then shall my passions all be love,
And all my powers be praise.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
